title: 💰 A $111B Hollywood mashup
body_text: It’s the one time of year when bulking season comes with a trophy. Fat Bear Week kicks off this week at Alaska’s Katmai National Park, where the internet gets to vote on which brown bear has done the most impressive job packing on the pounds ahead of hibernation. This year’s field is looking especially well-fed. One contender has been described as “just a balloon,” while another, Bucky, is “just a giant.” Stocks were mixed on Tuesday as oil prices continued their recent decline, falling for the fifth straight day on reports that the Saudis were close to restarting a critical pipeline that had been damaged by a Houthi attack last week. Paramount Skydance on Monday reached a settlement with a dozen states that had sued to block the firm’s acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery , paving the way for one company to own an enormous chunk of the media and entertainment market. The settlement removed the last remaining obstacle in closing the $111 billion deal , which would put Spongebob and Bugs Bunny under one roof (among many, many, many other things). Here is a recap of what the combined company would own: News: CNN and CBS, two of the largest broadcast news networks in the country, will be under one owner, along with The Free Press. The settlement calls for the formation of a “News Editorial Independence Board to establish guiding editorial and journalism principles for the combined entity’s news channels.” Television: The combined company will own more than a dozen major cable networks, including Nickelodeon, Cartoon Network, MTV, Showtime and BET just to name a few. Film studios: One company will now own Paramount Pictures and Warner Bros. The settlement requires it to release a minimum of 30 theatrical films per year in the first two years of the decree, increasing to 32 films per year for the following three years. Much of the settlement, led by California, focuses on ensuring the film industry continues employing people. Streaming: HBO Max and Paramount+ now share an owner. Oh and also: David Ellison, the CEO of Paramount Skydance, is the son of Oracle co-founder and executive chairman Larry Ellison. In a deal finalized earlier this year, Oracle now owns a 15% stake in TikTok’s US operations. Combined, the father and son have influence over a solid chunk of what Americans watch on their screens big and small. After a long courthouse saga, Hollywood’s newest mega-merger is going ahead — just with a few strings attached. Paramount and Warner Bros are not the first to take advantage of a relaxed antitrust environment under the Trump administration. But few deals concentrate quite as many household-name entertainment brands in one place. Paramount-Warner would put everything from CNN and CBS to HBO, MTV, SpongeBob, Bugs Bunny, Harry Potter and Transformers inside the same corporate empire. The states that sued argued that this kind of consolidation could mean fewer movies, higher prices and fewer jobs. Rather than break up the deal, the settlement tries to put guardrails around it: Paramount has pledged to invest in film production and release a minimum amount of movies per year. More and more people are “managers” now, but only supervising AI agents. This leaves them with the snazzy title but no pay bump or opportunity to actually practice what they’re good at, Business Insider reports. That’s how much wealthier Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg got on Monday as investors celebrated the company’s new Muse AI agent, Yahoo Finance reports . GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen bought roughly $26.4 million worth of shares, according to a regulatory filing made public on Monday . Novo (previously known as Novo Nordisk ) told CNBC the company is mulling M&A opportunities. The Ozempic maker is on the hunt for its next slate of blockbuster drugs. SpaceX winding down Falcon 9, the world’s busiest rocket, is driving a rocket supply crunch, the Wall Street Journal reports . title: 👴 100 years young
body_text: A so-called “Lego bandit” was arrested last week after a high-speed pursuit through the streets of Nassau County, Florida, as police officers uncovered $20,000 worth of stolen Lego sets across the region in recent months. Alongside the 12 expensive Lego sets that the Florida man had made off with in his latest toy heist last Monday, police also seized suspected methamphetamine, fentanyl, and crack cocaine from the alleged offender’s U-Haul van, suggesting that the suspect was perhaps interested in more than just block trading… Stocks had a great start to the week, with the S&P 500 finishing Monday up about a point and a half. Okinawa, a group of around 160 islands off the south coast of Japan with a population of ~1.5 million people, has long been established as one of the world’s major longevity hubs. The residents’ mostly plant-based diet; their strong sense of purpose, or “ikigai;” and a tendency to command strong social networks were all cited as key reasons behind the island group’s status as one of just five official global “ blue zones ” — areas where life expectancies far outlast international averages, with disproportionate swaths of the population reaching 100 years of age or older. Zoom out a little further, though, and it becomes apparent that elements of Okinawa’s recipe for a long and healthy life have clearly been catching on across the mainland, too, as Japan’s centenarian population reaches yet another record high. According to figures published by the Japanese Ministry of Health, Labour, and Welfare last week, the number of nationals who are 100 years old or above has risen to 107,677 as of September 1, 2026. For context, that’s up almost 8,000 from the year before, and the figure has risen almost nine times from the turn of the century, when Japan’s centenarian population sat at just ~13,000. Japanese women account for a staggering 88% of the 100+ cohort, mostly reflecting the impact of World War II on males of the generation, as well as the fact that they traditionally worked in more physically demanding fields, and tended to drink and smoke more than their female counterparts. Given that Japan’s overall population peaked in 2008, this latest demographic stat out of the land of the rising average age is another signifier that the nation’s top heavy population problem isn’t going anywhere fast. Indeed, while Kenichiro Ueno, the nation’s health minister, announced that he was “delighted that so many people are living long, healthy and active lives,” it also speaks to the “existential crisis” that authorities have outlined, with Prime Minister Sanae Takichi labeling the aging population combined with its declining birthrate as a “ quiet emergency .” Doomer discussions around AI and its potentially (likely?) grave consequences for the Future Of Humanity have grown louder of late, but as far as the rise of robots that look and act like us goes, humans might be able to rest slightly easier… for now, at least. Last year, there were just 7,000 humanoid robot shipments around the world, per figures that the International Federation of Robotics shared with Reuters before publication. As Reuters noted, humanoid bots (those that are designed to resemble mankind and operate autonomously in human environments) represent a mere fraction of the overall robot population. Regardless of that fact, 7,000 still seems pretty low — it’s less than half of the 20,000 figure that BofA Global Research had forecasted for 2025. It’s also very far off the tallies that the BofA has predicted in the years to come, suggesting that the uprising of anthropomorphic robots might be a sprint, rather than a marathon. That might give anyone who’s seen any of the viral clips of their current running capabilities even more peace of mind. That’s how many centenarians there were in the US at the latest official count in 2020 — that meant that just two in every 10,000 Americans had hit 100, per US Census Bureau data published in 2025 . The figure had increased by 50% from when the bureau had run the numbers in 2010, when just 53,364 people in America had made it to the milestone birthday or further. Hollywood ending: Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount Skydance rose yesterday on reports that a settlement had been reached with California and other states that were initially hoping to block the proposed merger. Apple is paying out $250 million to settle claims from disgruntled customers who said the iPhone maker failed to deliver the AI-upgraded Siri it had promised to deliver — complainants have until December 21 to submit their claims. Any weight you can lose, I can lose better… Novo Nordisk today announced that CagriSema, its new experimental weight-loss drug, outperformed Lilly’s rival offering in late stage trials involving diabetes patients. title: 🛢️ Big Oil’s Venezuela comeback
body_text: Cats: famously good at hiding. Apparently, entire species of them are, too. Scientists have discovered a new species of spotted wild cat in Bolivia after a 10-year-old feline named Tigrino — previously mistaken for another type of tiger cat — turned out to have distinct DNA. So far, he’s the only confirmed living member of his species. For US oil majors, Venezuela went from “uninvestible” to investable in nine months. On 3 January, the US captured then-Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro in a military operation in Caracas. He is now in a Brooklyn jail where he faces drug trafficking charges. President Trump said the US would "run" and Venezuela moving forward and “fix oil infrastructure.” At the time, Exxon CEO Darren Woods said at a televised White House meeting that Venezuela was “ uninvestible .” US oil majors were not initially eager to jump back into Venezuela, where several of them say the government still owes them billions of dollars for seizing their assets after nationalizing the oil industry in 2007. A lot has changed since then. Last month, the White House announced a deal in which the US gets majority control of more than 65 billion barrels of proven oil reserves in Venezuela. On September 2, Chevron said its joint venture partnerships in Venezuela ​would invest more than $7 billion to more than double oil ⁠output to 600,000 barrels per day over the next five years. (Chevron, notably, said it received the right to international arbitration as part of its new contract ​terms, which would protect it if it has another dispute with the government.) In a euphemism-packed statement titled “ a turning point for Venezuela ,” Chevron said: “For years, regulatory uncertainty and restrictive investment terms made many projects difficult to justify, leaving significant resources undeveloped. Chevron believes that recent reforms and updated agreements have changed that equation, creating a stronger foundation for investment in a region where the company has operated for more than a century.” Last week, Continental Resources signed a preliminary deal with Venezuela’s state-owned oil company to explore one of the country’s biggest oil fields. The company is led by Harold Hamm, a Trump ally. More will likely follow: ExxonMobil is close to a deal to invest in Venezuelan oil fields after more than two decades away from the country, the Wall Street Journal and Reuters reported last week . While officially about “drug trafficking,” the capture of Maduro ultimately meant the US has access to the largest proven oil reserves in the world. US oil companies were burned by Venezuela’s in the past and were cautious about making their way back in, especially considering the billions of dollars of investment needed to improve the country’s infrastructure. But increasingly, it seems the Trump administration has succeeded in changing the calculus — and convincing American oil companies to drill, baby, drill. 🏈 MNF: Tonight New York takes on Los Angeles, with the Giants taking on the Rams in a game that will decide, once and for all, if the Rams completely and permanently messed up their sleep schedules with their catastrophic Melbourne travel fiasco.
